events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship Team to protect the forested areas in Powell's Cove Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been made possible with funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

events.description: New location for September. Forest Fridays are meeting at Classic Playground, not the Learning Garden.Help restore the woodland edge at Van Cortlandt Park. Volunteers remove the invasive shrubs and vines crowding out young native trees - multiflora rose, bush honeysuckle, porcelain berry, jetbead and ivy - and tend a small native planting put in this June. Hand tools only. Tools, gloves and guidance provided; no experience needed.Dates include Fridays weekly from September 4th - September 25th. Dates are 9/4, 9/11, 9/18, and 9/25.Meet at the public restroom building inside Classic Playground, at Van Cortlandt Park South and Gouverneur Avenue. The worksite is right at the playground, so latecomers can find us.Wear long sleeves, long trousers and sturdy closed-toe shoes. Bring water. Ages 15+ welcome; minors need a waiver.Sign up on Bloomerang

events.description: Volunteer with NYC Parks for Trees Count! At each event you will receive a tote bag with all the materials needed to count trees. Returning volunteers are welcome, and will receive additional giveaway items such as shirts, books, and hip bags as supplies last. Next, we'll provide a 30-minute training session that includes the basics of tree identification and how to measure and assess each tree. Using our Tree Census app, you’ll split up into different zones within the park to start counting trees! After completing your first training event, you are welcome to continue counting trees on your own in smaller parks across the city. For your comfort and safety, please bring water and wear closed-toe shoes to this program.

events.description: Bryant Park's first-ever Brass Festival brings three incredible incredible brass ensembles to the main stage. From Brass Queens' female-led upbeat horns, to Aberdeen's inventive jazz/indie rock blend, and finishing with the New Orleans-born, Grammy-nominated New Breed Brass Band, this high-energy celebration of modern brass is the perfect way to herald in the end of summer. New Breed Brass Band fuses NOLA’s fertile brass band tradition with Caribbean, hip-hop, and modern R&B in the vein of Bruno Mars and Anderson .Paak. The explosive group makes music by and for the Crescent City’s next generation: joyful, vital and unstoppable. New Breed Brass Band is led by drummer Jenard Andrews, son of Tremé trumpet legend James Andrews and nephew of New Orleans scene lynchpin Trombone Shorty. Under Trombone Shorty’s tutelage a new sound was born, and audiences took notice.The band has toured North America and Europe and opened for The Fray, Blackalicious and Dr. John. With the band’s debut album, 2023’s Made In New Orleans, New Breed is hewing a new path for 21st century second-lines, and everyone’s invited to join the procession.Aberdeen is a Brooklyn-based horn band known for its soulful melody-driven instrumental arrangements. Aberdeen's music is about community; a large collective of musicians featuring Allison Philips on trumpet, Olivia Hughart, Jared Yee, Mackenzie McCarthy, Brian Plautz & Stephen Chen on saxes, Jacob Melsha & Jasmi Perales on trombones, Shubh Saran on guitar, Ronnie Lanzilotta on bass and Ross Pederson on drums. Aberdeen's albums Downpour and Held Together showcase their energetic, massive, one-of-a-kind sound.Hailing from Brooklyn, NY, the award-winning Brass Queens are a female-led brass band featuring all-female horns with a sound that sits right at the intersection of the Big Apple and the Big Easy. Their music is deeply inspired by and pays homage to the New Orleans brass band tradition while injecting the upbeat, multifaceted energy of their New York home into each performance. Brass Queens tour regularly across the country and internationally, increasing the visibility of female musicians in the industry.Bryant Park Picnic Performances presented by Bank of America is a free outdoor festival that welcomes all New Yorkers to experience the city’s vibrant arts and culture. The series provides a platform for extraordinary artists and serves as a vital outdoor venue for a wide array of New York’s cultural institutions.

events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)

events.description: Everyone’s favorite yoga program returns for summer 2026! From May 27 through September 16, join us for classes Tuesday mornings on the Upper Terrace, and Wednesday evenings on the lawn. Bryant Park Yoga presented by Halara is free to the public. Bring your mat and water and enjoy one hour of yoga with New York City’s top instructors. Please register for each class at our website online, or in person. Pre-registration is strongly encouraged. Those who pre-register opt in to receive updates on weather-related cancellations and other notifications. By pre-registering, you complete the waiver in advance and will receive weather-related updates.Please present your QR code from your registration confirmation email to the Bryant Park check-in staff. Check-in locations can be found at all four corners of the lawn. Each check-in location is marked with pink barricades or a pink tent. We recommend you arrive at least 15 minutes early so you have time to check-in and roll out your mat before instruction begins.Classes are cancelled only when it is deemed unsafe or uncomfortable for participants. Follow @bryantparknyc for day-of updates.All Bryant Park Yoga classes are free and open to the public! All levels are welcome, thanks to the skill of our experienced teachers.*Please note there will be NO CLASS on June 23 and June 30.

events.description: Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. Our knowledgeable NYC Parks staff train kids in sports such as basketball, ball hockey, kickball, flag football, pickleball, soccer, team handball, track and field, and volleyball. Contact accessibility@parks.nyc.gov or (212) 360-1430 for more information regarding accessibility.

events.description: Cai Sherley (he/him) is a Black trans poet-educator with roots in Boston, MA. Cai is a two-time Pushcart Prize nominee, with work published or forthcoming in Best New Poets, swamp pink, Peach Mag, and Tupelo, as well as the anthology I Feel Nothing Like Good: Poets Against Genocide from Taylor & Co Books. His work centers Black transmasculine life, past and present, in the United States, and has found homes at The Watering Hole, Brooklyn Poets, Tin House, LAMBDA, and the Fine Arts Work Center. Cai is a member of the Crossroads Writers Collective and Trans Corner Poets, and the proud stepfather of two sphinxes. He is the author of Out of Yearning, selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series.Charlie Lou Evans (he/they) grew up in a small town in New Jersey, went to college at Virginia Tech, spent two summers thru-hiking the east and west coast, and now lives in Bellingham, Washington. His first chapbook, Gay Sex, celebrates the liberating power of queer love and was released by Sibling Rivalry Press this June. He explores gender and sexuality through poetry and finds it most fulfilling when others see themselves in their work.JC Andrews (she/her) is a lesbian poet from Springfield, Arkansas. Her work can be found in Gulf Coast, The Massachusetts Review, Waxwing, and elsewhere. Her debut collection, Of an Ilk, was a finalist for the 2024 National Poetry Series and won the 2026 Yale Series of Younger Poets competition. It will be published with Yale University Press in April 2027. Her chapbook, Trillion Amber Trumpets, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in April 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Kaitlin Hsu ?? (she/her/?) is a queer Taiwanese poet who believes in a free Palestine. A 2025 Lambda Literary Fellow and 2024 Margins Fellow at the Asian American Writers Workshop, she has also received support from Brooklyn Poets, genARTS Silicon Valley, the Mendocino Coast Writers Conference, and more. She is the author of the chapbook Paper Dolls (Sibling Rivalry Press), selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series. Her work can be found most recently in A Public Space, Poet Lore, and Peach Mag. She currently works at Kaya Press as an associate editor and development coordinator.Toni Garcia-Butler (he/they) is a poet and community artist-educator rooted in Little Rock, Arkansas. He approaches his craft as a memory keeper, believing that poets and artists can be creative cultural archivists. His writing and art center the lived experiences of his people: Black, Fil-am, southern, trans/queer, and everyone existing within the intersections. As a facilitator, Toni encourages folks to empower themselves through DIY publishing/zinemaking, personal narrative, and creative joy. In 2025, Toni was named Best Poet in Arkansas by the Arkansas Times. His chapbook, D I Y Body, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in June 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Hosted by:Bryan Borland is the founding publisher of Sibling Rivalry Press and founding editor of Assaracus: A Journal of Gay and Queer Poetry. He is the author of multiple poetry collections, including Brotherful, a finalist for the Thom Gunn Award for Gay Poetry, and DIG, a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award in Gay Poetry and Stonewall Honor Book as honored by the American Library Association. His most recent book is Listen, Kid: Selected and New Poems (2010-2026).Kay Ulanday Barrett is a poet, essayist, and cultural strategist. Barrett is a 2024 Disabled Futures fellow awarded by The Ford Foundation, Mellon Foundation, and United States Artists. They are the winner of the 2022 Foundation for Contemporary Arts Cy Twombly Award for Poetry, a winner of the 2022 Next Book Residency with Tin House, a James Baldwin Fellowship at MacDowell, residencies at Baldwin for the Arts, and Millay Arts awarded by Lambda Literary. events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. events.description: Join us for the premiere of Alison Nguyen’s new film Prior Occupants, co-commissioned by High Line Art and CHANEL Culture Fund. Following the screening, Nguyen will be joined in conversation by High Line Art Associate Curator, Taylor Zakarin, to discuss her practice and this exciting new work.This event is rain or shine. Although advance RSVP is full, walk-up visitors will be welcome if the event is not at capacity._____________________________________________________________________________________________________Alison Nguyen is a visual artist working across video, installation, performance, and sculpture. Using approaches of speculative fiction, documentary research, and embodied performance, Nguyen creates works that reconsider how narratives operate within the individual, the institution, the archive, and within the politics of cultural memory.In her compelling new film for High Line Originals, co-commissioned with CHANEL Culture Fund, Nguyen explores the obscure nuclear history of Westbeth Artist Housing’s building—the former headquarters for Bell Laboratories, a research facility tied to the development of communication technologies and, later, the atomic bomb. Inspired by a severed fragment of the original High Line freight rail left embedded in Westbeth’s facade, and the High Line’s own history of transformation, Nguyen reflects on the historical narratives that persist—and those quietly erased—within sites of adaptive reuse.Long before Westbeth’s conversion into a historic public housing community for artists in 1970, the site was occupied by Western Electric and later Bell Labs—a crucible of innovation where critical cinema, telecommunications, and military technologies were researched, including components later used in the development of the atomic bomb. Both Bell Labs and Westbeth Artist Housing are places created to pursue large, even utopian ideals. In the case of the former, technological innovation; in the case of the latter government-funded artist housing. Prior Occupants explores what remains of the pursuit of these ideals, how the surrounding architecture has shaped its inhabitants, and the contradictions of present-day Westbeth in the context of the High Line’s surrounding neighborhood.Prior Occupants is an assemblage of audiovisual material including sculpturally re-filmed archival documents, choreographed performance sequences, and layered fragments of audio interviews with the very residents and architects who have shaped Westbeth and the High Line. Through this collage of voices and textures, the artist explores individual and collective relationships to place, technological acceleration, and mortality, and foregrounds the ways in which the structures of the past quietly haunt our future-present. Questioning the relationship between ruination and cultural production, the work asks: What does it mean to stage the decay of an industrial past within public environments and within public artist housing? What role does nature play in these acts of preservation? Nguyen’s film weaves together infrastructure, memory, and technology to consider how the legacy of the nuclear age continues to shape our collective experiences, and positions the High Line not just as a space for leisure, but as an active conduit of our historical consciousness.Part of High Line Channel, High Line Originals is High Line Art’s commissioning program for artists working in time-based media. This initiative invites emerging or underrecognized US-based artists, nominated by a trusted group of contemporary curators, to submit a proposal for a new video work that considers the context of the park in a meaningful way and will resonate with our diverse audience.High Line Originals launched in 2019 with Tourmaline’s Salacia, which is now held in the Museum of Modern Art’s permanent collection. Other past commissions include Onyeka Igwe’s The Miracle on George Green (2021), and Alicia Mersy’s NYC Wisdom (2024). In 2025, High Line Art partnered with CHANEL Culture Fund, and together co-commissioned Frank WANG Yefeng’s Groundless Flower – ? (2025).

events.description: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

events.description: Fire in the Heart of the City details the riveting story of what happened when a tragic fire in Greenwich Village threw Adolph Ochs, the ambitious new publisher of the New York Times, and Rose Schneiderman, a defiant young labor organizer, against each other in a momentous conflict. Following the 1911 Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire-the worst disaster New York City had ever experienced up to that point-a significant feud emerged between New York’s wealthy elite and labor rights’ activists over who should organize the city's response: a nascent charity sector led by the city's wealthiest bankers or the reform-focused unions of Lower Manhattan. Fire in the Heart of the City is an absorbing portrait of an extraordinary moment in the formation of modern American charity, casting new light on its profoundly dangerous and misunderstood legacy.David Conrad-Pérez is a historian and former journalist whose work examines the forces that shape the media, philanthropy, and public life. He serves as research director for the Center for Media & Social Impact at American University. A former producer for New York Public Radio’s On the Media and Public Radio International’s The World, he has also written for The New York Times, Reuters, and Columbia Journalism Review. He holds a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania’s Annenberg School for Communication.

events.description: Lindy hop and jitterbug followed by Latin jazz and salsa.Alfredo De La Fé is an internationally acclaimed violinist, best known for revolutionizing the role of the violin in salsa and Latin music. His virtuosity and pioneering approach have helped to establish him as a leading figure in Latin jazz and salsa, blending traditional classical techniques with the vibrant energy of Afro-Cuban and Caribbean rhythms.A musical prodigy, Alfredo began studying classical violin at the age of 7 under the guidance of his father. After moving to New York, he began performing with local salsa bands, experimenting with how the violin could be integrated into the genre. Alfredo's big break came when he joined Eddie Palmieri’s band in the early 1970s. Alfredo has released over 30 albums, including the Grammy-nominated Alfredo. He has collaborated with a multitude of legendary artists, from salsa icons Eddie Palmieri, Tito Puente, and Celia Cruz to Latin jazz pioneers Mongo Santamaría, Papo Lucca, Ray Barretto, and Willie Colón. His ability to adapt his violin to different contexts—from traditional Afro-Cuban music to jazz fusion—has earned him acclaim across multiple genres.As one of the pioneers of the Latin violin, Alfredo De La Fé has also taken on the role of educator, sharing his knowledge and passion with aspiring musicians. He has conducted workshops and masterclasses around the world, teaching students about the technical aspects of violin playing, as well as the rhythmic and melodic intricacies of Latin music. His influence can be seen in the growing presence of the violin in contemporary salsa and Latin jazz ensembles, with many young musicians citing him as a major influence on their development.The George Gee Swing Orchestra spearheaded the modern swing resurgence nearly four decades ago. Headlining regularly at Lincoln Center’s Midsummer Night Swing, the swing big band was a favorite of famed Savoy swing dancer Frankie Manning having performed a long series of dance events in his honor in New York City, Boston, Chicago, San Francisco and Tokyo! Lindy Hoppers around the country and world are big fans of George Gee’s high-energy shows! Catch them weekly at SWING46 Jazz & Supper in Times Square.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)

events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

events.description: Join Jes Good Rewards Children's Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a hands-on volunteer day cleaning up the garden! GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. events.description: The monarch butterfly is one of North America’s most iconic and beloved species. With vibrant orange-and-black wings, the butterflies can be observed in NYC’s parks and gardens from late spring until fall, when they take to the sky to make a remarkable migration, traveling south to the mountains of Mexico where they will spend the winter. Unfortunately, monarch populations have declined significantly in recent decades for a number of reasons, including the loss of milkweed plants--the only plant monarch caterpillars eat. But there’s good news: we can help monarchs by planting native milkweed species and restoring and connecting pollinator habitat throughout their migratory flyway. During this workshop, learn about the monarch’s life cycle, its impressive multi-generational 3,000 mile migration, and how to help them thrive in NYC green spaces. Attendees will be able to take home native milkweed or butterfly nectar plants for their gardens.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.description: This living history event will commemorate the 250th Anniversary of the only Peace Conference held during the American Revolution on September 11th, 1776.Saturday, September 12th, 11 am to 4pm At Conference House & Park Great Lawn, 7455 Hylan Blvd, Tottenville SI 10307 $10.00 Each; Children under 12 $5.00,  children 5 years and under FREE.  ALL Scouts in uniform admitted for FREE and get a Conference House Patch! Outdoor Event. Opening Ceremony featuring the Staten Island Bagpipers at 11 am.The highlight of the event is a reading of an excerpt of the Peace Conference at 2pm. Board members portraying all of the key figures discussing the many issues that were faced back then, in an effort to put an end to the Revolutionary War. The day includes costumed Colonial dancers who are accompanied by 18th Century music.There will be an outdoor Museum exhibit and visitors can take a peek at the vegetables growing in the Colonial Kitchen Garden.Various 18th century craftspeople demonstrate Colonial era trades such as woodworking, coopering, tin smithing, black smithing beekeeping, chair caning, spinning, wampum making techniques and weaving and quilting. Visitors see demonstrations and learn about various crafts.Among other activities children have the opportunity to make kites (in homage to Ben Franklin) and to try their hand at the art of calligraphic writing. Colonial cooking is demonstrated at the outdoor open hearth fires by the dedicated members of the Conference House Auxiliary. They will share Colonial recipes for cornbread and soup. Modern day snacks will be available for purchase.

events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

events.description: Jackie O and John Perreault at Snug Harbor: A Literary Portrait Featuring guest speakers:   Wayne Koestenbaum, Author of Jackie Under My Skin and Andy Warhol: A Biography Daniel Rothbart, artist currently exhibiting at Snug Harbor and friend of John Perreault On the 50th anniversary of Snug Harbor opening its doors to the community after the transition from Sailors’ Snug Harbor into Snug Harbor Cultural Center on September 12, 1976, join us for an intimate literary reading that traces the legacies of two essential figures within the Snug Harbor story.  When: Saturday, September 12, 2026 |  3:00 PM – 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building CAdmission: Free (Registration Required) Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and John Perreault were each instrumental in shaping the story of Snug Harbor Cultural Center. In the mid-1970s, when after being saved from demolition, the former sailors’ home faced an uncertain future, Kennedy toured the site on behalf of the Municipal Art Society, lending her influence to the preservation effort. Later, she famously piloted the Staten Island Ferry back to Manhattan. A decade later, Perreault became one of the first professional curators at the Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art at Snug Harbor (1985–1989), where he championed Staten Island artists such as Julia Healy, Elizabeth Egbert, and Cynthia Mailman, while also presenting off-island figures including Nancy Spero, Judy Chicago, and Gillian Jagger. Though they moved in different circles, Andy Warhol forms a compelling link between them. As chief art critic for The Village Voice in the 1960s and ’70s, Perreault became a key chronicler of Pop Art and a close friend of Warhol—at one point speaking with him nightly for nearly two years. Warhol’s Jackie series, based on images of Kennedy  before and after the assassination, was among the works Perreault reviewed with particular attention. Jackie herself maintained a cordial relationship with Warhol and shared friends in New York’s art and fashion worlds, including Halston and Truman Capote. In the summer of 1972, she and her, Lee Radziwill, along with their children, stayed at Warhol’s Eothen estate in Montauk. Another point of resonance between Jackie O and John Perreault is fashion. Kennedy helped define 1960s style through the so-called “Camelot” look—pillbox hats, tailored shift dresses, and Oleg Cassini-designed suits—later evolving into her signature “Jackie O” ensemble of oversized sunglasses, headscarves, and Gucci handbags. Perrealut, in turn, approached fashion as an artistic medium. In 1969, with Hannah Weine and Eduardo Costa, he co-organized the Fashion Show Poetry Event, a hybrid of runway, performance, and text. Twenty artists designed garments worn by fellow artists and poets, accompanied by live music and recorded readings written specifically for each look. Participants included Andy Warhol, James Lee Byars, Alex Katz, Marisol, Claes Oldenburg, and James Rosenquist, among others.    Artist and writer Wayne Koestenbaum is the author of Jackie Under My Skin, a book about Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and Andy Warhol: A Biography. In 1998, he curated an exhibition titled Bathroom at the Thomas Healy Gallery, exploring themes of the body, voyeurism, and personal territory, which included work by John Perreault. Artist and writer Daniel Rothbart met Perreault in 1999, and the two maintained a close friendship and ongoing creative dialogue until Perreault’s death in 2015, frequently writing about one another’s work. Perreault included Rothbart in The Ritual Feast at KK Projects in New Orleans in 2008. Drawing on personal experience and longstanding engagement with their subjects, Koestenbaum and Rothbart will reflect on the intertwined legacies of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and John Perreault, and consider how each helped shape the cultural history of Snug Harbor. This literary reading is part of our Serpentine Sybils public art exhibition on view at the Pond and the Glasshouse

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

Attendees will have access to information and support related to housing, mental health, health care, benefits, financial assistance, community engagement and other essential services. events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. events.description: Chelsea Whitton is the author of Bear Trap (Dancing Girl Press, 2018) and Wonder Wheel, published by LSU Press in March of this year. She holds a PhD from the University of Cincinnati and an MFA in Poetry from The New School. Her poetry and prose have appeared in many of print and online publications, including Beloit Poetry Journal, Copper Nickel, Cream City Review, Poetry Ireland, The Atlanta Review, and Forklift-Ohio. Her work has been a finalist for the Gearhart Prize, and the Frost Place and Adrienne Richard awards for poetry. She is the recipient of the 2018 Sandy Crimmins National Poetry Prize. Raised in the Carolinas, she spent her twenties in New York and now lives in Southwestern Ohio, where she teaches at the Art Academy of Cincinnati.Dilruba “Ruba” Ahmed is the author of Bring Now the Angels (Pitt Poetry), with poems featured in New York Times Magazine, The Slowdown, and Poetry Unbound.  Her debut book, Dhaka Dust (Graywolf Press), won the Bakeless Prize.  Her poems have appeared in Kenyon Review, New England Review, Ploughshares, and Virginia Quarterly Review.  Her work has also been anthologized in Best American Poetry, Halal If You Hear Me, New Moons: Contemporary Writing by North American Muslims, They Rise Like a Wave: An Anthology of Asian American Women Poets, and elsewhere. Ahmed received The Florida Review’s Editors’ Award, a Dorothy Sargent Rosenberg Memorial Prize, and the Katharine Bakeless Nason Fellowship awarded by the Bread Loaf Writers Conference. In 2021, she joined the faculty at Warren Wilson College’s MFA Program for Writers.Matthew Yeager’s poems have appeared in American Poetry Review, Poem-a-Day, and elsewhere, as well as numerous anthologies, including Best American Poetry 2005, 2010, and 2024, The Strategic Poet, and Twenty Years of PoemoftheWeek.com. “A Big Ball of Foil in a Small NY Apartment,” his micro-budget short film, was an official selection at eleven film festivals in 2009-2010, picking up three awards. His “Poem to First Love” has appeared in online features in O, The Oprah Magazine, Good Housekeeping, Newsweek, Brides, and elsewhere. Other distinctions include the Barthelme Prize in short prose and multiple fellowships to both MacDowell and Yaddo. The co-curator of the KGB Monday Night Poetry Series from 2011-2017, Yeager’s first book, Like That (Forklift Books, 2016), received a starred review from Publishers Weekly. He teaches adjunct and lives in Cincinnati with his wife Chelsea Whitton and their twin sons Hank and Pete.Sahar Muradi is author of the collection OCTOBERS, selected by Naomi Shihab Nye for the 2022 Donald Hall Prize for Poetry and a finalist for the National Poetry Series. She is author of the chapbooks [ G A T E S ], Ask Hafiz, and A Garden Beyond My Hand, and co-editor of two anthologies: One Story, Thirty Stories: An Anthology of Contemporary Afghan American Literature, and EMERGENC(Y): Writing Afghan Lives Beyond the Forever War, An Anthology of Writing from Afghanistan and its Diaspora. Her writing has been supported by Asian American Writers’ Workshop, Bethany Arts Community, Blue Mountain Center, Kundiman, and Sustainable Arts Foundation. Sahar directs the arts education programs at City Lore and dearly believes in the bottom of the rice pot.

events.description: Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. Our knowledgeable NYC Parks staff train kids in sports such as basketball, ball hockey, kickball, flag football, pickleball, soccer, team handball, track and field, and volleyball. This program covers basic and more advanced techniques.  Summer Sports Experience is a drop-in program recommended for children ages 8-14. Participants can stop by for one or more sessions, but kids who stay for the whole program will get the most benefit from it. Occasionally a Summer Sports Experience program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions.Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. Summer Sports Experience is not a childcare program, and NYC Parks is not responsible for the well-being of attendees. For more information, please visit nyc.gov/parks.  Contact accessibility@parks.nyc.gov or (212) 360-1430 for more information regarding accessibility.

events.description: Celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Battle of Harlem Heights, the first Patriot victory of the American Revolution.The Morris-Jumel Mansion, then known as "Mt. Morris" or the summer home of British Military Officer Colonel Roger Morris and family, became the headquarters of General George Washington, his officers, and troops for five weeks in the fall of 1776. Almost immediately after establishing the headquarters, Washington and his troops would be faced with another opportunity to emerge victorious in a war in which they had only been defeated in up until this point.The Battle of Harlem Heights is a largely unappreciated milestone in American military history. This engagement on upper Manhattan Island on September 16, 1776 marked the first successful battlefield outcome achieved by George Washington’s troops in the quest for independence from Great Britain and presaged the gradual emergence of an effective fighting force among the citizen-soldiers who made up the Continental Army and bore the brunt of young America’s struggle for political and economic self-determination. The cooperative effort of regiments from New England, Maryland, and Virginia—whose men lacked any sense of national identity before the Revolution—indicated the potential for this fledgling army to cohere around a common national purpose and affiliation and become the primary instrument for gaining American independence. David Price, author of The Battle of Harlem Heights, 1776 joins the Mansion to take a deep dive into this small but extremely important moment in history on it's 250th anniversary. About the speaker:David Price has authored five books about America’s War of Independence, including a trilogy about the winter 1776/77 “Ten Crucial Days” campaign. His last book in that trilogy, Winning the Ten Crucial Days, was named an Honorable Mention for the Fraunces Tavern Museum Book Award and a Finalist for the Army Historical Foundation Distinguished Writing Award. The other volumes in the trilogy are The Road to Assunpink Creek and Rescuing the Revolution. In addition, he has authored John Haslet’s World and The Battle of Harlem Heights, 1776. The latter is part of the Westholme Small Battle series and was accepted into the permanent collection of the Connecticut Museum of Culture and History. David is a recipient of the National Society of the Sons of the American Revolution Bronze Good Citizenship Medal, as well as its Certificate of Appreciation, in recognition of his work as an author, speaker, and historical interpreter at Washington Crossing Historic Park in Pennsylvania and Princeton Battlefield State Park in New Jersey. He has written extensively for the prestigious, peer-reviewed Journal of the American Revolution, as well as The Journal of America’s Military Past, Discover Concord magazine, The Bann Disc journal, and the Swan Historical Foundation newsletter. David holds degrees in political science from Drew University and Rutgers University, and worked as a nonpartisan research analyst for the New Jersey Legislature for thirty-one years. He lives in Lawrence Township, NJ. More information about David and his work can be found at dpauthor.com.

events.description: A concert version of an original musical connecting the Creole cultures of Réunion Island, Puerto Rico, and New Orleans.Réunion Island-based theater company Tilawcis brings their latest work, Flamboyants!, on a North American tour this fall. This work of documentary theater with music explores the remarkable intersections of Creole culture and identity between the geographically distant communities of Réunion Island, New Orleans, and Puerto Rico through music, storytelling, and gorgeous projections.Five languages are spoken on stage, and nearly a dozen instruments are played, fusing maloya, bomba, and Mardi Gras Indians songs. The piece explores themes of memory, identity, resilience, connection, and cultural transmission through the prism of the Creole experience. It shines a light on the richness of Creole cultures and their capacity to overcome historical oppression.Flamboyants! is a philosophy as much as it is a work of theater. Despite the 10,000 miles that separate Réunion from New Orleans, the Creole languages spoken in those two places are close linguistic cousins. Maloya musicians use the same Canna indica seeds in their kayamb instrument (a rectangular rattle made of sugar cane tubes) as bomba musicians use to create maracas in Puerto Rico. While the ties between these cultures have long been lost, their ancient, resilient wisdom, connected by the African diaspora, once again finds a home on stage in the celebration of Creole identity that is Flamboyants!Plot Summary: Réunion Island. While a cyclone rages, a man curses his name before throwing himself in the Indian Ocean. He has no idea what repercussions this action will have on the other side of the world. From Puerto Rico to New Orleans, Creole peoples will unite to teach him his true history. A work of musical theater, documentary and fictional, even fantastical in certain moments, Flamboyants! asks us to interrogate what stories our own names carry, the ways we’re interconnected, and the cultural resilience of those who fight to not be forgotten.

events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.description_html:
Under the Asthma-Free Housing Act (Local Law 55 of 2018), residential building owners in New York City are required to take steps to keep their buildings free of mice, rats, roaches and mold, collectively defined as Indoor Allergens. In this training, we will discuss owners' responsibilities to identify and eliminate indoor allergen hazards and other pests, as well as review the annual inspection requirements, when to use a licensed contractor, and how to clear HPD violations. Space is limited – please register now.

Topics include:

  • Eliminating and preventing infestations of mice, rats, cockroaches, and other pests;
  • Identifying current and future sources of mold;
  • Proper work methods for eliminating mold conditions and pest infestations;
  • Reviewing the city and state laws that underlie the Asthma-Free Housing Act;
  • Annual notification and inspection requirements and the annual Bedbug Filing (Local Law 69 of 2017); and
  • Steps to correct and remove HPD violations for Indoor Allergen Hazards.

events.title: Pests and Mold: An Owners Guide to Indoor Allergen Laws

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics.

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

This event includes paper shredding. Learn more about this event.

Navigating Housing Court can be daunting. Learn Housing Court processes, types of legal cases, and what to expect. It also addresses how tenants can seek recourse through Housing Court, such as to compel an owner to improve housing conditions. This class does not offer nor constitute legal advice.

Topics covered:

  • How to navigate Housing Court
  • Right to Counsel: free and low-cost legal assistance for tenants
  • Different types of cases: access, non-payment, housing part actions, and holdover evictions
  • Illegal lockouts
  • Where to seek help

This class presented by Housing Court Answers is intended for tenants and property owners.
